input.quote: Ono shall have the right, in accordance with this Section 2.2, to grant sublicenses under the Array Patents and Array Know-How to its Affiliates and to Third Parties
input.rationale: The grants at Sections 2.1(a)-(c) reach our Affiliates without any consent or notice condition (Section 2.2(a) sublicensing right to Affiliates; Section 2.1(b) manufacturing sublicences to Affiliates), which exceeds the fallback requirement that affiliates be covered on written notice. Section 18.9 lets either Party assign the Agreement, and with it the licences, without the other's consent "to an entity that acquires substantially all of the business or assets of the assigning Party, whether by merger, acquisition or otherwise", satisfying successor transferability in an M&A transaction. The licences are not revocable at Array's discretion: they run for the term and terminate only on defined grounds (uncured material breach under 13.3, insolvency, or our own election under 13.2), and on expiry they convert under 13.1 into "non-exclusive, fully paid- up, irrevocable, perpetual, royalty free licenses, with sublicensing rights". The bargain therefore sits at or above the fallback and we would not redline it. Shortfalls against the preferred position are noted only: contractor coverage is express for manufacturing ("may be extended by Ono to Third Party manufacturers for Manufacturing the Products on Ono's behalf") and Subcontractors are contemplated elsewhere, but engaging a Third Party as a Sublicensee or distributor of the Product requires Array's prior written consent.
